translations.title: In Memory of Josefina
translations.text:
I

Of what was a love, a sweetness
without equal, made of dreams and joy,
only cold ash remains
within this pale covering.

The orchid of fantastic beauty,
the butterfly in all its colors,
yielded their fragrance and splendor
to the fate that sealed my misfortune.

My memory rules over oblivion;
my grief draws her from her grave;
my faith summons her, my passion awaits her,

and I return her to the light, with that open,
springlike morning smile:
noble, modest, loving, and pure!

II

That I loved you beyond all others, you knew,
and the Lord knows it too; wandering ivy
never clings to a friendly wood
as your being joined my sorrowful soul.

In my memory your life persists
with the sweet murmur of a song,
and longing for your love eases
my grief, which resists oblivion.

Clear spring that never runs dry,
you live in me, and to my stern barrenness
your freshness mingles drop by drop.

You were the palm tree in my desert,
the gull upon my bitter sea,
and you will die only when I die!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: White Storks
translations.text:
A timid flock of storks,
gently folding their wings,
passed over the abandoned tower
in the light of dying twilight;

an hour when the Magician with his happy palette
pours beneath the radiant dome
pale shades of fleeting violet,
rippled by the wandering breeze.

Those birds unsettle me; in my soul
they rebuild my shattered joys;
they call up in my spirit the calm,
the solemn calm of better days.

The darkness of their eyes surpasses
even ebony's burning tones,
and their red-tinted beaks
join their alabaster throats.

The outline of their silken flanks
is a vague sign of mystical sadness,
calling to mind, when they stretch in sunlight,
the slow agonies of Whiteness.

With their garments of magical white,
with their languid, slender form,
their figures in the air resemble
the pale banner of Dream.

And if one, fleeing the claw that stalks it,
draws in its wing and stretches out its head,
it looks like a bow with a reddish arrow
that some hidden hand draws in the air.

In the glow of starlight,
in the sway of their weary flight,
they seem, beneath the concave vault,
blue bacchantes drunk on heaven...
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXIII: For a Glance, a World
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXII: How Does That Rose Live...?
translations.text:
How does that rose you have pinned
beside your heart survive?
Never before have I seen on earth
a flower upon a volcano.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXI: What Is Poetry?
translations.text:
“What is poetry?” you ask, fixing
your blue eyes upon mine.
“What is poetry?” And you ask me?
Poetry... is you.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXVIII: Feigning Realities
translations.text:
Feigning reality
with empty shadow,
Hope walks before
Desire.

And its lies,
like the Phoenix, rise again
from their ashes.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXXI: Dawn Is a Shadow
translations.text:
Dawn is a shadow
of your smile,
and daylight a ray
from your eyes;
but your soul
is winter night,
black and frozen.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XVII: Today the Earth and Heavens Smile on Me
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXVII: You Say You Have a Heart, and Only
translations.text:
You say you have a heart, and say so only
because you feel it beat;
that is no heart... it is a machine
that makes noise as it moves in time.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
